description: Play Tic Tac Toe 4x4 online for free. Four in a row wins on the bigger 4×4 board. Play vs the computer in 3 difficulties or 2 players, no download.
lede: Tic Tac Toe on a 4×4 board, where you need four in a row to win. The classic game (in [[tic-tac-toe]]) is a forced draw between good players; the bigger board has room for real attacks, traps and comebacks.

p: Players take turns placing their mark, X or O, on a 4×4 grid. The first to get four in a row across, down or diagonally wins. There are only ten winning lines: four rows, four columns and the two long diagonals. If all sixteen squares fill up without a line of four, the round is a draw.
In this version you are X against the computer. The first move switches every round, so sometimes the computer starts.

ol: Win: if you have three in a row and the fourth square is free, take it.
Block: if your opponent has three in a row, take the fourth square. Nothing else matters that turn.
Take squares that sit on three lines: the four centre squares and the four corners each belong to three of the ten lines. Side squares belong to only two.
Build a double threat: aim for a move that makes three in a row in two lines at once. Only one can be blocked.
Count the diagonals early. With only two of them, a diagonal quietly filling up is easy to miss.
p: On a 3×3 board perfect play always draws. On 4×4 a single mistake is not fatal, but a line of three with the fourth square free is a loaded threat: it must be answered at once. A few habits win games here:

dl: Mostly random. It sometimes spots a winning move and rarely blocks yours. Good for learning the bigger board.
Takes a win when it sees one and usually blocks your lines, but it only looks a couple of moves ahead, so a double threat can catch it.
Searches thousands of positions ahead before every move, inside a strict time budget. Very strong, but on the 4×4 board it is not perfect like the 3×3 version, so it can be beaten.

p: Three in a row on a small board is solved: two careful players always draw. Stretching the target to four in a row on a 4×4 board keeps the same simple rules but opens the game up, a little like Connect Four (1974) did for stacking games, and like Qubic, the 4×4×4 four-in-a-row game from the 1960s.
If you prefer the original, the classic 3×3 game is [[tic-tac-toe]].

Start with the original [[tic-tac-toe]], or play [[rock-paper-scissors]] and [[memory-match]] with a friend on one screen. More games for two are in [[cat:two-player|2 player games]], and more thinking games in [[cat:strategy|strategy games]].

faq: How is this different from normal Tic Tac Toe?
The board is 4×4 instead of 3×3 and you need four marks in a row to win instead of three. Everything else (turns, draws, modes) works the same way.
How do I play with a friend?
Open the options under the board and choose 2 Players. You take turns on the same device: X first, then O.
